stem: A nursing unit uses a dashboard to display selected quality measures over time. According to AHRQ quality-improvement guidance, what is a principal benefit of this dashboard?

options.A: It establishes the exact root cause of every adverse event without any additional event investigation.
options.B: It removes the need to select measures that are linked to the improvement goal and intervention.
options.C: It proves that any change in a metric was caused by the most recent intervention, regardless of other factors.
options.D: It summarizes important performance data so staff can identify gaps and trends against goals and share consistent information across organizational levels.

rationale: AHRQ states that dashboard reports present important data in summary form to make gaps in performance and trends against goals easier to identify and can share consistent information across multiple organizational levels. Therefore D is correct. A dashboard does not by itself establish root causes, so A is incorrect. B conflicts with AHRQ's requirement to choose measures linked to the improvement goal and intervention. C overstates what a dashboard can establish; AHRQ describes monitoring how interventions relate to changes, not proof that one intervention caused every observed change.
educational_objective: Use quality dashboards to make selected performance measures, gaps, and trends against goals visible for monitoring and shared improvement work rather than treating the display itself as proof of causation or root-cause analysis.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Using Measures to Monitor Progress in Improving Patient Experience
source_locator: Selecting Measures; Displaying Data — dashboard reports present important data in summary form to identify performance gaps and trend performance against goals; dashboards can share consistent information across organizational levels
source_claim_supported: AHRQ recommends selecting measures tied to improvement goals and interventions, visualizing and monitoring performance, and using dashboard reports to summarize data, identify gaps and trends against goals, and share consistent information across organizational levels.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7/PDF p.11: Participate in performance improvement activities; Use data to support client care and organizational decision-making
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality measurement and performance improvement
correction_summary: Retained the dashboard construct but replaced simplistic secrecy/positive-only distractors with three realistic overclaims about dashboards: root-cause determination, measure-selection replacement, and causal proof. Anchored the final answer to the exact March 2026 AHRQ dashboard wording. Difficulty remains easy.

audit_findings.option_A: Wrong but plausible — dashboards display measures but do not substitute for event investigation/root-cause analysis.
audit_findings.option_B: Wrong but plausible — AHRQ explicitly says measures should be linked to the larger goal and intervention.
audit_findings.option_C: Wrong but plausible — monitoring association over time is not equivalent to proving causation.
